**2.1 Income Limits**
- Annual household income from all sources shall not exceed INR 3,00,000 for applicants belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) category.
- For applicants under the Low-Income Group (LIG) category, the annual household income ceiling shall be INR 6,00,000.
- Income shall be computed on the basis of the preceding financial year's income tax returns, salary certificates, or such other proof as may be required by the SRA Cell.

**2.2 Residency Requirement**
- The applicant must have been a resident of the slum area for a continuous period of not less than five years immediately preceding the date of application.
- Residence shall be established through documentary evidence, including but not limited to ration cards, voter identification, or utility bills in the applicant's name.

**2.3 Documentation Requirements**
- Applicants shall submit the following documents along with the application form:
  - Proof of identity (Aadhaar card, passport, or driving licence)
  - Proof of residence (ration card, electricity bill, or rent agreement)
  - Income certificate issued by the competent authority
  - Photographs of the dwelling unit
  - Declaration form regarding family composition
- The SRA Cell may call for additional documents as deemed necessary on a case-by-case basis.

---

**3. Version 2.0 (Effective 15-07-2021) – Amendment No. 1**

Amendment No. 1 was issued on 15-07-2021, primarily to address procedural ambiguities and streamline the application process. The following changes were made:

**3.1 Revision of Income Limit**
- The income ceiling for the LIG category was revised from INR 6,00,000 to INR 7,50,000 per annum.
- The EWS income ceiling remained unchanged at INR 3,00,000 per annum.

**3.2 Clarification on Family Definition**
- The term "family" was clarified to include the applicant, spouse, dependent children, and dependent parents residing in the same dwelling unit.
- Income of all family members shall be aggregated for the purpose of determining eligibility.

**3.3 Additional Documentation Requirement**
- Applicants are now required to submit a self-declaration regarding any property owned elsewhere in the State of Maharashtra.
- This declaration shall be on the prescribed format annexed to the application.

**4. Version 3.0 (Effective 01-04-2022) – Amendment No. 2**

Amendment No. 2 was issued on 01-04-2022, incorporating feedback from the Membership Sub-Committee and the State Government. The changes are detailed below:

**4.1 Residency Requirement Relaxation**
- The continuous residency requirement was relaxed from five years to three years for applicants who can demonstrate that they were displaced due to a natural calamity or a government infrastructure project.
- Such applicants shall provide a certificate from the concerned revenue authority or municipal corporation.

**4.2 Income Verification Procedure**
- The SRA Cell shall verify income declarations through the State's integrated database, wherever available.
- In cases where the database is not accessible, the applicant may be required to appear for a personal interview before the Verification Officer.

**4.3 New Clause: Ineligibility on Grounds of Prior Availment**
- An applicant who has previously availed of any housing benefit under any central or state government scheme shall not be eligible under the SRA scheme, unless the prior benefit was for a dwelling unit that was destroyed due to fire, flood, or other natural calamity.

- The total annual income of the applicant family shall not exceed INR 4,50,000 (Rupees Four Lakh Fifty Thousand only) for eligibility under the SRA scheme.

- The income ceiling shall be reviewed by the State Government every two years, or earlier if warranted by inflationary trends. Any revision shall be notified through a separate amendment to these criteria.

**6.2 Components of Income**
- Income shall include, but not be limited to: salaries, wages, business or professional earnings, agricultural income, rental income, pension, interest on deposits, dividends, and any other recurring receipts.
- One-time receipts such as gratuity, provident fund settlement, or insurance claims shall not be treated as income for the purpose of this ceiling, provided they are not received on a recurring basis.
- Income from all sources, whether taxable or non-taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1961, shall be aggregated for determining eligibility.

**6.3 Verification of Income**
- The SRA Cell shall verify income declarations through the State's integrated database, wherever available.
- In cases where the database is not accessible, the applicant may be required to appear for a personal interview before the Verification Officer.
- The Verification Officer shall have the authority to call for any additional documents, including bank statements, Form 16, or audited accounts, to substantiate the declared income.
- Any discrepancy found between the declared income and verified income shall render the application liable for rejection, and the applicant shall be given an opportunity to explain the discrepancy within fifteen days of notice.

The following documentation requirements pertain to redevelopment schemes under the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) and are not part of the SRA eligibility criteria. - All documents shall be self-attested by the applicant.

documents.title: SRA Eligibility Criteria – Version History
documents.content:
**2.1 Income Limits**
- Annual household income from all sources shall not exceed INR 3,00,000 for applicants belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) category.
- For applicants under the Low-Income Group (LIG) category, the annual household income ceiling shall be INR 6,00,000.
- Income shall be computed on the basis of the preceding financial year's income tax returns, salary certificates, or such other proof as may be required by the SRA Cell.

**2.2 Residency Requirement**
- The applicant must have been a resident of the slum area for a continuous period of not less than five years immediately preceding the date of application.
- Residence shall be established through documentary evidence, including but not limited to ration cards, voter identification, or utility bills in the applicant's name.

**2.3 Documentation Requirements**
- Applicants shall submit the following documents along with the application form:
  - Proof of identity (Aadhaar card, passport, or driving licence)
  - Proof of residence (ration card, electricity bill, or rent agreement)
  - Income certificate issued by the competent authority
  - Photographs of the dwelling unit
  - Declaration form regarding family composition

Amendment No. 1 was issued on 15-07-2021, primarily to address procedural ambiguities and streamline the application process. The following changes were made:

**3.1 Revision of Income Limit**
- The income ceiling for the LIG category was revised from INR 6,00,000 to INR 7,50,000 per annum.
- The EWS income ceiling remained unchanged at INR 3,00,000 per annum.

**3.2 Clarification on Family Definition**
- The term "family" was clarified to include the applicant, spouse, dependent children, and dependent parents residing in the same dwelling unit.
- Income of all family members shall be aggregated for the purpose of determining eligibility.

**3.3 Additional Documentation Requirement**
- Applicants are now required to submit a self-declaration regarding any property owned elsewhere in the State of Maharashtra.
- This declaration shall be on the prescribed format annexed to the application.

**6. Income Eligibility Criteria (As per Amendment No. 3, Current Version)**

**6.1 Annual Income Ceiling**
- The total annual income of the applicant family shall not exceed INR 4,50,000 (Rupees Four Lakh Fifty Thousand only) for eligibility under the SRA scheme.
- The Sharma Family's annual income is 450000 INR as per the eligibility criteria. Record status: current. This figure is recorded in the SRA Cell's verification database and forms the basis for determining the family's eligibility category under the current version of these criteria.
- The income ceiling shall be reviewed by the State Government every two years, or earlier if warranted by inflationary trends. Any revision shall be notified through a separate amendment to these criteria.

**6.2 Components of Income**
- Income shall include, but not be limited to: salaries, wages, business or professional earnings, agricultural income, rental income, pension, interest on deposits, dividends, and any other recurring receipts.
- One-time receipts such as gratuity, provident fund settlement, or insurance claims shall not be treated as income for the purpose of this ceiling, provided they are not received on a recurring basis.
- Income from all sources, whether taxable or non-taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1961, shall be aggregated for determining eligibility.

**6.3 Verification of Income**
- The SRA Cell shall verify income declarations through the State's integrated database, wherever available.
- In cases where the database is not accessible, the applicant may be required to appear for a personal interview before the Verification Officer.
- The Verification Officer shall have the authority to call for any additional documents, including bank statements, Form 16, or audited accounts, to substantiate the declared income.
- Any discrepancy found between the declared income and verified income shall render the application liable for rejection, and the applicant shall be given an opportunity to explain the discrepancy within fifteen days of notice.

---

**7. Documentation Requirements (For Redevelopment Schemes – Not Applicable to SRA)**

The following documentation requirements pertain to redevelopment schemes under the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) and are not part of the SRA eligibility criteria. These are reproduced here for the convenience of applicants who may be eligible for either scheme and wish to compare requirements before applying.

**7.1 List of Documents**
- Proof of identity: Aadhaar card, PAN card, or passport.
- Proof of residence: Electricity bill, property tax receipt, or ration card.
- Proof of ownership or tenancy: Sale deed, leave and license agreement, or rent receipt for the last twelve months.
- No-objection certificate from the society, where applicable.
- Photographs of the existing dwelling unit (interior and exterior).
- Undertaking on stamp paper regarding the number of occupants.

**7.2 Submission Format**
- All documents shall be self-attested by the applicant.
- Documents in languages other than English, Hindi, or Marathi shall be accompanied by a certified translation.
- Original documents shall be produced for verification at the time of the personal interview, if called for.

**7.3 Processing Fee**
- A non-refundable processing fee of INR 500 shall be payable at the time of submission of the application for redevelopment schemes. This fee is not applicable to SRA applications, which are processed without any fee.

**Version 1.0 (Effective 01-01-2021)**

This version was the initial issue of the eligibility criteria for SRA schemes under the jurisdiction of the SRA Cell. It was prepared following consultations with the Membership Sub-Committee and was circulated to all registered tenant associations and cooperative housing societies (CHS) within the operational area.

**1. Income Limits**

- Monthly household income from all sources shall not exceed INR 25,000 for applicants residing in the island city and INR 20,000 for applicants residing in the suburbs.
- Income shall include salary, wages, business income, pension, and any other regular receipts.
- Income certificates issued by the office of the Deputy Collector or the Competent Authority shall be valid for a period of twelve months from the date of issue.

**2. Residency Requirements**

- The applicant must have been a resident of the structure proposed for redevelopment for a continuous period of at least three years prior to the date of application.
- Residence shall be verified through the electoral roll, ration card, or any other document as may be prescribed.

**3. Documentation**

- Proof of identity, proof of residence, proof of income, and a declaration of family composition.
- All documents shall be self-attested.

**4. Ineligibility**

- Applicants who own any other residential premises in the city or suburbs of Mumbai shall not be eligible.
- Applicants who have availed of any other housing scheme of the State Government shall not be eligible.

**Version 2.0 (Effective 15-06-2022)**

**Amendment Record**

This amendment was issued to revise the income limits and to incorporate clarifications regarding the treatment of irregular income. The amendment was necessitated by the rise in the cost of living and the recommendations of the Membership Sub-Committee.

**Amended Clauses**

- Clause 1 (Income Limits): The monthly household income limit for applicants residing in the island city is revised from INR 25,000 to INR 30,000. The limit for applicants in the suburbs is revised from INR 20,000 to INR 25,000.
- Clause 1 (Income Limits): Income from irregular sources, such as casual work or seasonal employment, shall be averaged over a period of twelve months for the purpose of determining eligibility.

**Unchanged Clauses**

All other clauses of Version 1.0 remain in force. The residency requirements and documentation requirements are unchanged.

**Version 3.0 (Effective 01-04-2023)**

**Amendment Record**

This amendment was issued to extend the residency period and to provide a more detailed list of acceptable documents. The amendment also introduced a provision for the verification of documents through the database of the concerned authorities.

**Amended Clauses**

- Clause 2 (Residency Requirements): The continuous period of residence required is extended from three years to five years prior to the date of application.
- Clause 3 (Documentation): The list of acceptable documents is expanded to include the following:

- Aadhaar card (for proof of identity)
  - Voter ID card (for proof of identity and residence)
  - Electricity bill or water bill in the name of the applicant or a family member (for proof of residence)
  - Rent receipt for the last twelve months, where applicable (for proof of residence)
  - Bank statement for the last six months (for proof of income)
  - Salary slip for the last three months, where applicable (for proof of income)
  - A declaration on plain paper regarding the family composition and the number of occupants of the dwelling unit.
